openings.claim: Route retaining-strap tension through removable strip-mounted clearance stops. Coupling might limit the supplied corner-lift failure while retaining the hatch; physical synergy is unmeasured.
openings.delta: A retains against separation; B sets repeatable clearance. Change their interface: padded, removable rim saddles carry strap attachments and strip/bolt stops outside the seal. The stop reacts strap compression before excessive corner loading. Release straps and lift all carriers clear; cord retains recoverable loose parts outside the opening.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: ordinary strap friction plus independently useful spacers explains improvement. Coupling predicts intact A×B produces less pull displacement and opposite-corner lift than an otherwise identical link-broken assembly, beyond the gains observed for A alone and B alone. Equal results defeat a coupling claim; increased lift or seal damage defeats this design.
openings.probe: First check rim access, attachment reach and stop placement with ruler; abandon fabrication if supplied materials cannot form stable removable saddles. Compare untreated baseline, A alone, B alone, intact A×B and link-broken A×B. For link-broken, preserve straps, stops, carriers and clearances but redirect strap reaction onto the rim, bypassing stops. Use two trials per baseline/parent control and three per complete configuration: twelve closure/pull trials, including one card-disturbed trial in each complete configuration. Record 20 N displacement, corner lift, reopening time, seal tears, fabrication/setup minutes and reset burden. This screens coupling only; it cannot establish ten-cycle durability within this allocation.
assumptions: Unspecified rim geometry permits padded saddles and both force paths using supplied strips, bolts and 250 mm straps within ninety minutes.
Parent-ablation controls are permitted alongside the two alternative complete joint configurations; otherwise the five-state comparison exceeds the configuration allowance.
Stops can contact outside the seal without permanent deformation; attachment stability and useful stop clearance remain unknown.

assessment: Keep the original ten-cycle, 1 mm, 20 N and thirty-second outcome as acceptance criteria. This uncertain screening hypothesis grants no deployment permission or proven performance. Setup feasibility, trial-cap interpretation and durability remain unresolved.
